title: Another Grameen Bank office set on fire, in Muksudpur, Gopalganj
excerpt: Marchers burned the office beside Muksudpur police station, which was also set on fire, adding to a wave of arson against the microfinance bank.
content:
Marchers vandalised and set fire to a Grameen Bank office in Farid Mia Super Market in Muksudpur, Gopalganj, on Thursday (19 November), bdnews24.com's Bangla edition reported. The market stands beside Muksudpur police station, which was vandalised and set on fire at around 11:30am the same day. No one was reported hurt at the police station, which had been empty since Wednesday evening.

Local people said hundreds of activists of the banned Awami League and its affiliated groups marched in the area, the paper reported. The house of Selimuzzaman Selim, the BNP MP for Gopalganj-1, in Kashiani was vandalised and set on fire, and the Dhaka-Khulna and Dhaka-Barishal highways were blocked with felled trees. The report gave no figures for damage at the bank office.

Why it matters

Grameen Bank said last week that 22 of its branches in 16 districts had been set on fire or targeted between 10 and 17 November, and the UN has called for all the violence to be investigated (see our earlier report). Branch offices hold borrowers' records and savings, and staff and members, most of them poor women, bear the risk. Other microfinance NGOs in the same areas may need to review security.

What to watch

Arrests and statements from Grameen Bank and the police, and whether the attacks spread to other microfinance providers.
